html:
The 23 nuclear explosions set off by the United States at Bikini Atoll, in the Marshall Islands, between 1946 and 1958. The people of Bikini were moved away and have still not been able to go home safely.

After the Second World War the United States held the Marshall Islands. In early 1946 a navy officer asked the 167 people of Bikini to leave for the good of mankind. They were moved first to a smaller atoll, then to the island of Kili.

The first tests, Operation Crossroads in July 1946, aimed atomic bombs like those of the Hiroshima and Nagasaki attacks at a fleet of old warships. In 1954 the hydrogen bomb Castle Bravo, far stronger than expected, spread fallout over inhabited atolls and over the crew of a Japanese fishing boat. The outcry fed the movement against nuclear tests.

Some Bikinians returned in the 1970s but had to leave again in 1978 after tests showed high radiation in their bodies. The bikini swimsuit, launched in Paris days after the first test, took the atoll's name.
